claims.text: TC4 (Ti6Al4V) has a dual-phase alpha-plus-beta microstructure in its standard condition.
Standard TC4 has low surface hardness.
Standard TC4 has poor friction and wear properties.
TC4 will be friction-stir processed at approximately 800 rpm and a traverse speed of 100 mm/min using a non-consumable tool.
A thin, pre-placed layer of TiC nanoparticle slurry will be incorporated during friction stir processing.
The specified process will produce a modified surface layer approximately 1–2 mm deep.
Solid-state friction stir processing will avoid high-temperature effects on the TC4 substrate.
Controlled pre-placement and stirring will produce uniform TiC nanoparticle incorporation.
The intervention will form a fine-grained, recrystallized TC4 surface layer.
TiC nanoparticles will be uniformly embedded in the processed surface layer.
Severe plastic deformation during friction stir processing causes dynamic recrystallization and microstructural refinement.
Embedded TiC nanoparticles reinforce the surface and impede wear.
Grain refinement and TiC reinforcement will increase surface hardness relative to untreated TC4.
The treatment will reduce wear rate under high-contact-stress conditions relative to untreated TC4.
The bulk properties of TC4 will remain largely unaffected by the surface treatment.
The predicted improvements are limited to the approximately 1–2 mm-deep friction-stir-processed layer under the specified processing parameters.
The magnitude of improvement depends on uniform nanoparticle dispersion and minimization of process-induced defects.

The hypothesis is falsified if FSP-plus-TiC samples fail to exceed both untreated and FSP-only controls by a statistically significant hardness improvement, exemplified by greater than 10%, together with a measurable wear-rate decrease.
